newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech flood damage to crops at least CZK 1.5bln.
newsitem.headline: Czech flood damage to crops at least CZK 1.5bln.

text.p: The Czech Agriculture Ministry on Friday said a preliminary estimate for crop damage from massive flooding in the eastern part of the country was about 1.5 billion crowns.
"So far the figure is 1.5 billion crowns damage to the harvest," ministry official Marcela Dvorakova told Reuters, adding that more information would be collected and released on Tuesday.

Milos Kordac, assistant to the president of the Czech Agrarian Chamber, said data collected from most of the affected districts so far put damage to harvests at at least 1.4 billion crowns, with about 130,000 hectares of agricultural land affected.
Asked whether the situation would lead to a significant increase in imports, Kordac said: "We think not. The damage is not so large as to deteriorate the balance of the market."
However, he added that reports have not yet been delivered from some hard-hit areas where phones do not work or farmers have not yet had chance to inspect their land.
Both said the figure excluded damage to fields due to mud, erosion and other factors.
The flooding, which is reported to have claimed at least 32 lives, was moving south on Friday while water levels were coming down on upper streams of the affected rivers.
Poland, Slovakia amd Austria have also been hit by the rain-induced flooding. --Jan Lopatka, Prague Newsroom, 420-2-2423-0003
